successCriteria.description: The Notification domain interface is exported from the notification module's model file with the exact field set and string-literal-union types declared in the reconciled architecture (id, recipientId, type, title, message, relatedEntityType, relatedEntityId, status, createdAt, readAt) — a reviewer can confirm the interface compiles under strict TypeScript and matches the reconciled entity shape.

The INotificationRepository interface is exported and declares all five operations (create, findByRecipient, markAsSent, markAsRead, createBatch) with the correct return types, plus the CreateNotificationDto type — a reviewer can confirm the interface is implementable and the DTO excludes the server-managed fields (id, createdAt, readAt) and defaults status to PENDING.

NotificationRepository.create persists a row into the notifications table via a parameterized INSERT and returns the mapped Notification with camelCase fields; the repository uses the shared pg pool by default and accepts an optional Queryable client for transaction participation.

NotificationRepository.findByRecipient queries notifications for a given recipientId and returns the mapped Notification[] (empty array when none exist), ordered consistently (e.g. by created_at DESC) so the recipient inbox is deterministic.

NotificationRepository.markAsSent sets the notification status to SENT and returns the updated Notification (or null when no row matches); NotificationRepository.markAsRead sets status to READ and read_at to the current timestamp and returns the updated Notification (or null when no row matches).

NotificationRepository.createBatch performs a single multi-row INSERT for a non-empty DTO array and returns the mapped Notification[]; for an empty input array it returns [] without issuing any database query.

The notification module barrel (index.ts) re-exports Notification, INotificationRepository, NotificationRepository, and CreateNotificationDto so downstream modules (leave-request) can import the notification module only through its public entry point.

Jest unit tests under tests/unit/modules/notification/ cover the repository: create mapping, findByRecipient (populated + empty), markAsSent (hit + null), markAsRead (hit + null), createBatch (multi-row + empty no-query), and the custom-client constructor — all passing under the project's ts-jest configuration.

constraints: no-any: the Notification model, repository interface, DTO, and repository implementation must use `unknown` with type guards (e.g. `Record<string, unknown>`) rather than `any`; strict TypeScript with strict null checks must pass.

no-direct-db-outside-repository (GP-001): all database access for notifications goes through NotificationRepository; the repository is the only component that issues SQL against the notifications table.
All SQL must use parameterized placeholders ($1, $2, …) — no string-interpolated user values — to prevent SQL injection; timestamps use NOW() server-side, not client-supplied Date values.

The repository constructor must accept an optional Queryable client (Pick<Pool,'query'>) defaulting to the shared pool, so notification writes can participate in a caller-owned transaction per the Transaction Contract.

Modules import from each other ONLY through their declared public entry point (index.ts); the notification module must not reach into another module's internals, and downstream consumers must import notification only via its barrel.
outOfScope: NotificationService and INotificationService — the service layer that orchestrates notification fanout is not part of this phase; only the model, repository interface, repository implementation, and barrel are in scope.
Fastify routes / controllers / HTTP endpoints for notifications — no transport layer is built in this phase.

Database migration / DDL for the notifications table — the conceptual schema is defined in the reconciled architecture; this phase assumes the table exists and only implements the repository against it.
Integration tests against a real PostgreSQL instance — only Jest unit tests with a mocked pool are in scope for this phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: Lifecycle is strictly PENDING → SENT → READ → ARCHIVED; a newly created notification always starts in PENDING status (the create path never accepts a caller-supplied status), and readAt is null until the notification transitions to READ.

Every notification is anchored to exactly one related entity: relatedEntityType is constrained to 'LeaveRequest' and relatedEntityId is a non-null identifier, so a notification can always be traced back to the leave lifecycle event that produced it.

A notification has exactly one recipient (recipientId) and one type from the leave-transition set (LEAVE_SUBMITTED, LEAVE_APPROVED, LEAVE_REJECTED, LEAVE_CANCELLED); the type is immutable after creation and determines the notification's semantic meaning.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Persists one notification row with status defaulting to PENDING and created_at set server-side (NOW()); read_at is null on creation. Rejects with a typed error if the underlying query fails. Not idempotent — each call produces a distinct row with a new id.

Returns all notifications for the given recipient, ordered deterministically (newest first); returns an empty array (never null) when the recipient has no notifications. Read-only — no state change, no audit record required.

Transitions the notification status to SENT and returns the updated Notification, or returns null when no row matches the given id. A state-changing write — callers that wrap this in a business operation must ensure an audit record is produced at the service layer (GP-002 is enforced outside this repository).

Transitions the notification status to READ and sets read_at to the current server timestamp (NOW()); returns the updated Notification, or null when no row matches the given id. Idempotent in effect — re-marking an already-READ notification re-stamps read_at but does not error.

Performs a single multi-row INSERT for a non-empty array and returns all created Notifications; for an empty input array returns [] without issuing any query. Each row defaults to PENDING status. Not idempotent — repeated calls with the same DTOs produce duplicate rows.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: NotificationRepository must follow the established repository shape from AuditRepository: a private `db: Queryable` where `type Queryable = Pick<Pool,'query'>`, a constructor `constructor(client?: Queryable) { this.db = client ?? pool }` importing `pool` from `../../shared/db/connection`, a snake_case row interface, a `rowToNotification` mapper converting snake_case columns to camelCase fields, and a `COLUMNS` constant joined string used in SELECT/RETURNING clauses.

createBatch must mirror the LeaveBalanceRepository.createBatch pattern: early-return [] for empty input without querying, build per-row value placeholders with incrementing $N parameters, issue a single multi-row INSERT … RETURNING ${COLUMNS}, and map all returned rows via the row mapper.

The notification barrel (index.ts) must match the audit/leave-balance barrel convention: re-export the model interface from the model file, the repository interface and DTO(s) from the repository-interface file, and the repository class from the repository file — no logic, only re-exports.

The notification repository unit test must follow the audit/leave-balance test convention: jest.mock the shared db connection module returning `{ pool: { query: jest.fn() } }` cast to Pool, a `makeRow(overrides)` helper with snake_case defaults, a duplicated COLUMNS constant for exact-SQL assertions, beforeEach resetting the mock and constructing `new NotificationRepository()`, and a custom-client constructor test asserting the provided client's query is used instead of the pool.

The Notification entity shape and the notifications table conceptual schema (columns: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at; indexes on recipient_id, status, and (recipient_id, status)) must match the reconciled architecture exactly — the repository's row interface and COLUMNS constant must align with these columns, and the model interface must match the reconciled Notification attributes.

integrationPoints.why: NotificationRepository imports `pool` from the shared db connection as its default Queryable, matching every other repository; this is the only external dependency of this standalone supporting module.

The leave-request service will inject INotificationRepository to create notifications on lifecycle transitions (LEAVE_SUBMITTED, LEAVE_APPROVED, LEAVE_REJECTED, LEAVE_CANCELLED); this phase establishes the contract (interface + DTO) that Phase 10 consumes via the notification barrel.

The repository writes against the notifications table whose recipient_id is a foreign key to employees.id; create/createBatch must supply a valid recipientId so the FK constraint is satisfied at the database level.
